sections.title: Away or toward
sections.content: English has "go" and "come", and so does Hungarian. *Megy* is for travelling to somewhere else, and *jön* is for travelling toward the speaker, or toward the place where the other person is. If Anna is at the museum and Meg says she is on her way, Meg says *Jövök*. The person always shows in the ending, so you need the right form for *én*, *te*, *ő*, *mi*, *ti* and *ők*.

sections.title: How you come
sections.content: The vehicle or company ends in *-val/-vel*. *Bicikli* ends in *i*, a neutral vowel, so every vowel in it is neutral and it takes *-vel*: *biciklivel*. For "on foot" there is no ending: *gyalog*.
Meg and Anna are friends on the phone: if Anna is already at the museum, Meg says *Jövök a múzeumba* (I am coming), not *Megyek*. Think of *jön* as "toward you".
